title_en: How Far Is It in Chinese

sentences.en: On Sunday, older brother wanted to ride his bike to the park, and I wanted to go too.
I asked him: "Is the park far or not far from our house?"
Older brother said: "Not far, but I don't know exactly how far either."
We asked dad, and he said: "The park isn't far from here — ten minutes by bike and you're there."
We were happy, and right away got on our bikes and went out.
After ten minutes of riding, we really did reach the park, and older brother laughed and said: "See, it's not far at all!"

quiz.q: What is the writer asking her brother?
a: Whether the park is far from their house
Whether he wants to ride a bike

quiz.q: Who explains that the bike ride only takes ten minutes?
What does older brother say when they arrive at the park?

grammar.p: A 离 B + 远/近（measuring distance between places）
grammar.e: 离 states the distance from one place to another.
grammar.x: 公园离我们家远不远？— Is the park far or not far from our house?

grammar.e: 有多远 asks for the precise distance, once you already know it's 'far' in some sense.
grammar.x: 我也不知道有多远。— I don't know exactly how far it is either.

grammar.e: Repeating 远 with 不 in between makes an A-not-A question asking simply whether something is far.
grammar.x: 公园离我们家远不远？— Is the park far from our house or not?
